title: Coroner's inquest called into immigration detainee Abdurahman Hassan's death at Peterborough Regional Health Centre
subtitle: A coroner's inquest has been ordered into the death of a mentally ill diabetic Somali refugee at Peterborough Regional Health Centre (PRHC) while he was in immigration detention at the provincial jail in Lindsay.
article: A coroner's inquest has been ordered into the death of a mentally ill diabetic Somali refugee at Peterborough Regional Health Centre (PRHC) while he was in immigration detention at the provincial jail in Lindsay.
Abdurahman Hassan, 39, died at the hospital on June 11, 2015 after a police-escorted transfer from Central East Correctional Centre for medical treatment.

The inquest is mandatory under the Coroners Act, according to a release issued Friday by Dr. Paul Dungey, the regional supervising coroner for the Ministry of Community Safety and Correctional Services' regional office in Kingston.
The inquest will examine the circumstances surrounding the death, according to the release. The jury may make recommendations aimed at preventing similar deaths.
The date, location and presiding coroner will be announced later.
Tings Chak, a member of the watchdog group End Immigration Detention Network, wasn't particularly happy with the announcement.
Inquests can take one to two years, she said, and their recommendations don't necessarily have to be implemented.
She said in the time it will take to carry out an inquest, more detainees will die.
"We cannot wait a couple of years for answers or recommendations no none will follow," she said.

On Friday, Ontario's Special Investigations Unit (SIU) released results of a 13-month investigation into the death; it concluded that no charges against the two police officers involved are warranted.
The SIU investigated the death because two police officers were involved: One from Peterborough Police, and another from the Ontario Provincial Police (OPP).
The SIU report describes how the two officers restrained an agitated Hassan in a hospital room, at 1 a.m., while four nurses tried to clean him and his bedding of feces.
The report states that officer #1 - of the Peterborough Police - was limited to restraining the man's left arm while nurses attempted to clean him and the room.
There's no reason to think that had any "adverse affect" on the man's wellbeing, the report states.
The SIU report also states that officer 2 - of the OPP - used a towel to cover the man's mouth so he didn't bite or spit. The officer was also holding the man's head against the bed.

But the SIU concluded that the man's nose was unobstructed and no pressure was applied to the throat. Also, the man was snorting through his nose and yelling through the towel, indicating that he had no difficulty breathing.
What's more, the report states that the post-mortem exam ruled out mechanical asphyxiation as a cause of death.
Hassan had been in Canadian Border Services Agency custody for more than three years. He had severe schizophrenia.
He had been accepted as a refugee to Canada in the mid-1990s. He was jailed following an assault conviction in 2012, and then transferred to immigration custody.
A week after his death, immigration detainees at the Central East Correctional Centre went on a hunger strike in a show of solidarity.

About 60 immigration detainees in maximum-security detention at the Lindsay superjail and the Toronto East Detention Centre in Scarborough also went on a hunger strike Monday to protest conditions. It's slated to go for two weeks.

End Immigration Detention Network called on Immigration Minister Ralph Goodale this week to end indefinite immigration detentions. The group has posted an online petition. The group had also urged a coroner's inquest into Hassan's death last year.

The End Immigration Detention Peterborough group is planning a rally on Monday from noon to 1 p.m. outside the constituency office of Democratic Institutions Minister and Peterborough-Kawartha MP Maryam Monsef at 417 Bethune St. in support of the hunger strike and to back up the call to end indefinite immigration detention.
The protesters will be urging Monsef to take action to urge Goodale and the federal government to respond to the claims of the detainees on the hunger strike, according to a release.
